summary: This is the About page of FDIC.gov, the website of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, an independent agency created by Congress to maintain stability and public confidence in the nation's financial system. The page describes the FDIC's mission (insuring deposits, examining and supervising financial institutions, making large institutions resolvable, and managing receiverships), its five-person Board of Directors, careers, initiatives, and history since 1933. Much of the note is repeated navigation and news-slider boilerplate, which was ignored.
one_line: Overview of the FDIC's mission, leadership, careers, initiatives, and history as presented on its FDIC.gov About page.
key_facts: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) is an independent agency created by Congress to maintain stability and public confidence in the nation's financial system.

To accomplish its mission, the FDIC insures deposits, examines and supervises financial institutions for safety, soundness, and consumer protection, makes large and complex financial institutions resolvable, and manages receiverships.
The Board of Directors of the FDIC manages operations to fulfill the agency's mission.
Each member of the five-person FDIC Board is appointed by the President and confirmed by the Senate.
Since its creation in 1933, the FDIC has been an essential part of the American financial system.
In the 1920s and early 1930s, a rise in bank failures created a national crisis, wiping out many Americans' savings.
Since FDIC insurance began in 1934, no depositor has lost a single penny of insured funds due to bank failure.
FDIC-Insured Institutions Reported Net Income of $38.4 Billion in Fourth Quarter 2023 was a press release dated March 7, 2024.
FDIC Releases Economic Scenarios for 2024 Stress Testing was a press release dated February 15, 2024.
FDIC Unveils Immersive Timeline of Agency's History and Mission was an event dated February 15, 2024.
The FDIC describes itself as a pre-eminent source of U.S. banking industry research, including quarterly banking profiles, working papers, and state banking performance data.
The FDIC's initiatives include Trust through Transparency, Economic Inclusion, Community Banking, and Community Affairs.
The FDIC's Quarterly Banking Profile for Fourth Quarter 2023 was published as an event on March 7, 2024.
